intelligence.human_view: A cache-buster that doesn't bust the cache is worse than no cache-buster at all — it tells you the build is verified while showing you a different build. The `cb` parameter looks like proof: same URL, different `cb`, surely a different build. It isn't. The proof host serves the current build whatever `cb` you pass, so a "verification" by cb URL can pass on bytes you never built and fail on bytes you did. The fix is to verify from the source of truth: the branch's own blob, decoded through the GitHub blob API, byte-compared to what you curled — or an independently curled copy you control. Every captain's-eye verification in the day's log does it this way, and that is why their deliveries hold.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you have a magic box that always gives you the NEWEST toy, no matter which number you ask for! If you ask for toy number 5, you get the newest toy. If you ask for toy number 9, you still get the newest toy! So the number doesn't prove anything. To really check a toy, you have to look at the toy itself — not the number you asked for.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — if the shop always hands you the latest loaf no matter which one you point at, then pointing doesn't tell you which loaf you got. You have to look at the loaf itself. Same here: the little `cb` number doesn't change what comes back, so you check the real thing — the blob — not the number.
intelligence.naya_view: Verify by blob, never by cb. The proof host ignores `cb` — a cb URL can pass on bytes you never built.
